scene_summary: A small tiled room with a foreground bed, white shelving and cabinet, two floor lamps, an open wooden door, and a partially visible white furnishing at right.
overall_evidence: The reconstruction captures the main room layout and several distinctive furnishings, but changes the viewpoint and framing, simplifies important cabinet and right-side furnishing details, and omits much of the reference's floor color variation and warm lighting.

main_defects.description: The view is wider and less steeply downward: the bed occupies a different part of the frame, the door is narrower and farther back, and a large dark strip replaces the reference's left foreground framing.
main_defects.evidence: The reference door dominates the center-right foreground, while the reconstruction door sits against the back wall; the bed and wall boundaries also project differently.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some differences could reflect object placement or scale rather than camera alone.

main_defects.description: The cabinet's upper glazed openings and solid lower section are replaced by four opaque outlined panels.
main_defects.evidence: Two transparent-looking upper doors reveal the interior in the reference; the corresponding reconstruction doors are white and opaque.
main_defects.uncertainty: The exact construction of the reference glazing is not fully clear.

main_defects.description: The large white furnishing at right has a substantially different visible silhouette and occupies less of the image; its tall angled panel and raised rear shape are not reproduced clearly.
main_defects.evidence: A large slanted front panel fills the lower-right reference, whereas the reconstruction shows a smaller cropped rectangular form with horizontal trim.
main_defects.uncertainty: Both objects are cropped and their identity is uncertain; framing contributes to the difference.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction uses flatter, more uniform surfaces, especially on the gray floor, instead of the reference's mottled tan and gray floor appearance and more visible wood grain.
main_defects.evidence: The reference floor has prominent irregular tan and dark patches; the reconstruction floor is largely plain gray, and the door appears nearly uniform.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some reference floor variation may be a rug, lighting, or shadow rather than surface texture.

main_defects.description: The warm illuminated wall patches around the rear lamp are absent, giving the reconstruction more even and cooler lighting.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has bright warm pools above and beside the rear lamp, whereas the reconstruction wall is nearly uniformly lit.
main_defects.uncertainty: Exposure and rendering differences may contribute.

strengths: The tiled walls, white baseboards, foreground bed, and open paneled door are recognizable.
The broad white shelf and narrower cabinet sit side by side along the back wall, with a floor lamp to either side of the grouping.
The dominant pale furniture palette and the general bed-to-storage relationship are preserved.
uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. Differences in camera perspective and cropping can be difficult to separate from object size and placement. Partially occluded and off-frame geometry cannot be assessed.
